readerMoment: Has mapped their router and recorded an owned-host listener, but assumes NAT itself is the firewall and all private addresses are safe from outside traffic.
outcome: Can explain what an inbound firewall rule does, why NAT is not that rule, and identify how IPv6, a port forward or an existing connection can change the answer.
coreModel: Address translation changes a packet's destination, while a stateful firewall policy decides whether a new connection may cross a boundary.

teachingShape.startFromWhatTheySee: A listener on the owned machine and an incoming packet at the router
buildTheModel: Trace a reply to an outbound connection
Contrast unsolicited inbound with an explicit exception
teachingShape.traceOneExample: Same local listener under ordinary IPv4 NAT, an IPv4 port forward, and IPv6 with a stateful firewall
teachingShape.check: Given a new inbound packet and a rule, predict whether it is dropped or passed and what remains unknown
teachingShape.makeItTheirs: Reader labels their own boundary questions without changing any settings

requiredIdeas: NAT maps addresses/ports; lack of a mapping often blocks unsolicited IPv4 packets, but that is not the same as an explicit firewall policy.
A stateful firewall tracks connection state and may allow replies to outbound connections without allowing unrelated new inbound traffic.
Port forwarding, UPnP-created mappings, and firewall exceptions can allow a path to a listener; an existing listener alone does not prove reachability.
IPv6 may use globally routable addresses without NAT; the router's and host's IPv6 firewall policies still determine permission.
A host firewall, router firewall, address family, and network path are separate checks. Read settings on an authorized network before making a claim.
candidateAnalogies: An address label says where a package goes; the guard's policy says whether to admit it. A reply receipt can let a response back without letting strangers walk in.
visualNeeds: Side-by-side packet paths with a separate translation label and firewall decision gate

deliberatelyExcluded.what: Changing UPnP, port forwards or firewall rules
deliberatelyExcluded.why: The next page owns change control and outside testing.
Reachability still depends on stateful policy, host rules, routing and listeners.
Only owned or authorized configurations are discussed.

nextPagePressure: Having separated translation from permission, the reader can inspect and safely close exposure in the next page.
